title: Technology Sector Update for 09/18/2018: MRVL,ORCL,AAPL,CTSH,INXN
text:

Technology stocks continued to firm this afternoon when new tariffs on Chinese products announced Monday night exempted several Apple ( AAPL ) products, including the Apple Watch, AirPods and wireless headphones and prompting analysts at RBC Capital Markets to raise their price target for the company to $200. At last look, shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding almost 1.0% in value this afternoon while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising nearly 1.3%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Marvell Technology Group ( MRVL ) was higher in late Tuesday trading, rising almost 1.5%, after analysts at Goldman Sachs began coverage of the analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits manufacturer with a Buy investment recommendation and a $23 price target.
In other sector news:
(+) InterXion Holding NV ( INXN ) was almost 2.5% higher on Tuesday after the data center company announced plans for a EUR200 million ($233.6 million) private placement of its 4.75% senior notes due 2025. Net proceeds from the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, including certain expansion projects.
(+) Cognizant Technology ( CTSH ) was hanging on to a small gain Tuesday afternoon, easing from a more than 1% advance previously in the session that followed the technology services company announcing its acquisition of the Advanced Technology Group, a privately-held provider of customer and revenue management consulting and implementation services. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
(+) Oracle ( ORCL ) was narrowly higher Tuesday, overcoming a nearly 4% decline earlier today that followed the enterprise software firm reporting $9.19 billion in Q1 revenue, rising 1% over year-ago levels but still lagging the Capital IQ consensus by around $70 million. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.71 per share, topping Street views by $0.03 per share. Also helping lift Oracle shares in recent trade was the company authorizing a $12 billion increase for its stock buyback program and analysts at RBC Capital Markets raising their price target for its stock by $1 to $53 a share and reiterating their Sector Perform rating.
